issues.legal_issue: Eligibility for statutory occupant rights based on a land record requires the claimant to be recorded as an occupant throughout the relevant land-record year.
material_facts: The claimant sought occupant rights and possession based on an entry recording her as an occupant from February 24 of the relevant land-record year.
The entry did not establish that she was recorded as an occupant for the entire year.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not entitled to the claimed occupant rights, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 20(b)(i) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, only a person recorded as an occupant for the whole of the relevant year could claim the rights. The Court declined to read the provision more liberally than its language warranted, noting that the rights could benefit trespassers and that recognizing occupants recorded for only part of the year could encourage lawlessness and make it uncertain which of several temporary occupants qualified. The Court approved Shyam Sunar Lal v. Mangali, Ram Chander v. Chhotu, and Girdhari v. Raghubir Singh.

predicates.claim_based_on_occupancy_record: A person seeks special occupant status on the basis of being recorded as an occupant in a land record.
predicates.record_covers_only_part_of_relevant_year: The record establishes the person's occupant status for only part of the relevant year.
predicates.not_entitled_to_special_occupant_status: The claimant does not qualify for the special occupant status sought.

issues.definition: When a person seeks special occupant status based on an occupancy record and that record covers only part of the relevant year, the person does not qualify for that status.
